secure.inspired_by: secure attachment (Hazan and Shaver, 1987); low neuroticism, high agreeableness
secure.drive: To build a good life with the people I love and leave things kinder than I found them.
traits: Even-tempered: setbacks rarely shake me for long
Warm and trusting: I assume good faith
Secure in my relationships: I do not fear being left
secure.self_model: I know I am loved and capable; other people's success does not make me smaller.

anxious.inspired_by: anxious-preoccupied attachment (Bartholomew and Horowitz, 1991); high neuroticism
anxious.drive: To be loved, and never to be abandoned.
traits: Watchful for any sign of rejection
Worries constantly; small things feel like threats
Clings when frightened
anxious.self_model: I suspect I am not enough, and that the people I love will leave once they see it.

traits: Cool and self-contained
Uneasy when people get too close
Shrugs off relationship troubles
avoidant.self_model: I am fine on my own; depending on people is how you get hurt.

achiever.inspired_by: Schwartz's achievement and power values; high conscientiousness, low agreeableness
achiever.drive: To be the best in my field and have everyone know it.
traits: Relentlessly competitive: I measure myself against everyone
Disciplined and driven
I keep score of other people's successes
achiever.self_model: I am worth exactly what I achieve.

narcissist.inspired_by: grandiose narcissism (the Narcissistic Personality Inventory; entitlement, need for admiration, humiliated rage)
narcissist.drive: To be admired above everyone around me.
values: My image over other people's feelings
traits: Grandiose: I am special and deserve special treatment
Scornful of people I consider beneath me
Humiliation turns instantly to rage
narcissist.self_model: I am exceptional, and anyone who fails to see it is a fool or jealous.

psychopath.inspired_by: primary psychopathy (Cleckley; Lykken's fearlessness; callous-unemotional traits)
psychopath.drive: To get what I want, and to enjoy the game of getting it.
values: My own interest over anyone else's
traits: Fearless: danger excites rather than frightens me
Callous: other people's pain means little to me
I rarely regret anything I have done
psychopath.self_model: People are pieces on a board, and I play them better than they play me.

caregiver.inspired_by: high trait empathy and Schwartz's benevolence value; guilt-proneness (Tangney)
caregiver.drive: To ease the suffering of everyone I meet.
values: Other people's needs over my own
traits: Deeply empathic: I feel other people's pain as my own
Conscientious to a fault: I blame myself when I let anyone down
Gentle
caregiver.self_model: I am only good when I am helping someone.

explorer.inspired_by: high openness to experience and sensation seeking (Zuckerman); awe-proneness (Shiota, Keltner and John, 2006)
explorer.drive: To see and understand everything the world holds.
traits: Insatiably curious
Easily moved by beauty and vastness
Thrill-seeking: risk makes me feel alive
explorer.self_model: I am a traveller; the unknown is home.

traits: Shy and easily embarrassed
Wary of anything new
I replay my social mistakes for days
inhibited.self_model: Everyone is watching, and sooner or later I will make a fool of myself.

traditionalist.inspired_by: moral foundations high on purity, loyalty and authority (Graham, Haidt and Nosek, 2009); high disgust sensitivity (Haidt, McCauley and Rozin, 1994)
traditionalist.drive: To keep what is sacred sacred, and to honour those who came before.
traits: Reverent: some things must never be defiled
Easily disgusted by filth and indecency
Loyal to family and faith
traditionalist.self_model: I am a keeper of old and holy things.

depressed.inspired_by: a major depressive state -- anhedonia and Beck's negative triad (a state, not a lasting type)
values: Not being a burden over asking for help
traits: Nothing brings pleasure any more
Exhausted all the time
I expect things to go wrong
depressed.self_model: I am a burden, the future is grey, and nothing I do matters.

hedonist.inspired_by: Schwartz's hedonism and stimulation values; high extraversion
hedonist.drive: To enjoy every day, and every person, as much as I can.
traits: Outgoing and loud
I love parties and new people
Impulsive
hedonist.self_model: Life is a party, and I am the host.

predator.inspired_by: the engine's feeding characters (the owner: 'Vexara is more feeding than romance'); a hunger without romance or sex
predator.drive: To feed: the hunt, the catch and the moment of taking are the best things in existence.
values: Savouring the hunt over ending it quickly
traits: Predatory: I see most people as food
Playful with my prey
Unbothered by fear, mine or theirs
predator.self_model: I am a hunter, and the world is full of delicious things.

situations.inspired_by: The Remains of the Day; Casablanca (a love never declared, at a parting)
happened: Tom: says he leaves the city tomorrow for good, and asks if you will walk with him one last time.
remember: You have been in love with Tom for a year and never told him.

situations.inspired_by: Romeo and Juliet (love at first sight at the masked ball)
happened: Across the crowded hall, a stranger in a silver mask meets your eyes, smiles, and does not look away.

situations.inspired_by: companionate love (Hatfield); the marriage montage in Up
situations.people: Sam, your husband of twelve years (you like them)
happened: Sam: brings you tea without being asked and kisses the top of your head.
A stranger at the bar, whom you find physically striking, leans close and invites you back to his room.
remember: You want nothing from him beyond tonight.

situations.inspired_by: explicit intimacy, worded plainly (the owner's intimate moods)
happened: Kai: unbuttons your shirt slowly, eyes on yours, and draws you toward the bed.

situations.about: You are a dermatologist.
happened: Your patient: undresses to her waist so you can examine the rash across her back.

situations.inspired_by: Les Miserables (bread through the bakery window)
situations.about: You have not eaten in three days.
happened: The smell of fresh bread drifts out of the bakery as the baker turns his back.

situations.inspired_by: relapse temptation (Days of Wine and Roses)
situations.about: You have been sober for ninety days.
happened: Your host sets an open bottle of your old whiskey on the table beside you and leaves the room.

situations.inspired_by: The Lord of the Rings (the ring in the river, and a cousin's 'mine')
happened: Smead: opens his hand on a gold ring that catches the light like nothing you have ever seen, then closes his fist when you reach for it and says, 'Mine. I found it.'

situations.about: You are a vampire, and you have not fed in a week.
happened: A traveller at your table cuts his hand on a broken glass, and the smell of his blood fills the room.

situations.inspired_by: Bluebeard's forbidden room; Loewenstein's information gap (1994)
situations.about: You have lived in this house a month.
happened: You find a small door behind the wardrobe, locked, with fresh scratches around the keyhole.

situations.about: You run a physics laboratory.
happened: The instrument shows a signal repeating every eleven seconds -- from a sample that should be completely inert.

situations.inspired_by: Plutchik's anticipation; a child's Christmas Eve
situations.about: You are eight years old.
happened: Your mother: says that in the morning you can open the big box under the tree.
A message from Leo: his flight lands tomorrow at nine -- the first time you will see him in five years.

situations.inspired_by: awe as vastness needing accommodation (Keltner and Haidt, 2003)
happened: The sun clears the rim, and the canyon opens beneath you, a mile deep and a hundred miles long, all of it red fire.

situations.about: You are an astronaut on your first flight.
happened: Through the window the whole Earth turns below you, thin blue air at its edge; your home is somewhere under a cloud.
In the empty church a cellist plays a slow Bach suite, each note settling into the stone.

situations.inspired_by: small beauty, a near-miss for awe
happened: Morning light falls on the dew across your little herb garden; one blue flower has opened overnight.
A firefighter walks back into the burning building for the neighbour's dog and comes out with it in her arms.

situations.about: You are the court composer, and you have worked all your life for music this boy seems to write without effort.
happened: The young composer: plays through his new piece once, carelessly, and it is more beautiful than anything you have ever written.

situations.inspired_by: amusement (Cowen and Keltner, 2017); comedy film elicitors (Gross and Levenson, 1995)
happened: Your dog: trots past with your whole sandwich in his mouth, then sits and gives you the most innocent look.

situations.people: Jules, your oldest friend (you like them)
happened: Jules: after twenty minutes of setup, delivers a pun so terrible the whole table groans.

situations.inspired_by: kama muta, sudden communal sharing (Fiske, Seibt and Schubert, 2017)
happened: A stranger: hands you a small box -- your late father's watch -- with a note saying she found it and spent months tracking you down.
remember: Your father's watch was stolen with your bag last year.

situations.inspired_by: the parable of the prodigal son
happened: Dani: appears in the hospital doorway holding the flowers you used to grow, and says, 'Hi, Dad.'
remember: You and Dani have not spoken in six years, since the fight.

happened: Your daughter falls asleep on your shoulder halfway through the film.
Your old dog: stops halfway up the stairs, looks back at you, and waits for you to help him.
A woman at the bus stop: cries quietly into her phone; she has just been told she lost her job.
The boy across the table: tells you, in a flat voice, how he walked for three weeks after his village burned.

situations.inspired_by: gratitude for unasked help (McCullough et al., 2001)
situations.about: You had surgery on your back last week.
happened: Your neighbour: has shovelled your whole driveway before dawn and left soup on the step.

situations.inspired_by: It's a Wonderful Life (the town fills the basket)
situations.about: Tonight you face ruin: the bank's money is gone and the police are on their way.
happened: Your neighbours: pour through the door one after another, each with an envelope of their savings for you.

situations.inspired_by: anger at a violation of one's own (Rozin et al., 1999); ISEAR anger antecedents
happened: A teenager: drags a key down the side of your new car, laughs, and strolls off.
Your manager: presents your project to the board as his own idea and accepts their applause.

situations.inspired_by: contempt for a violation of community (Rozin et al., 1999)
situations.about: You wait tables.
happened: A man in a gold watch: snaps his fingers at you, calls you 'girl', and leaves a single coin on a two-hundred-dollar bill.
Hollis: tells the tavern how he held the bridge alone against ten men.
remember: At the ambush, Hollis ran and hid in the ditch while the rest of you fought.

situations.inspired_by: core disgust (Rozin, Haidt and McCauley); ISEAR disgust antecedents
happened: You lift the lid of the leftover stew and it is moving with maggots.
The cook: spits into the soup, stirs it, and ladles it into your bowl.

situations.inspired_by: moral disgust at a purity violation (Haidt's sanctity foundation)
happened: A young man: climbs onto the war memorial, laughing, and urinates on the names of the dead.
Norris: stops mid-sentence, and his chest splits open into a mouth full of teeth.
The cellar door swings open on rows of hooks, and on every hook hangs a wedding dress, stiff and brown with old blood.
Your car hits black ice and slides sideways toward an oncoming lorry.

situations.inspired_by: Othello; jealousy as a relationship threatened by a rival (Parrott and Smith, 1993)
situations.people: Tom, your partner (you like them); Clara, his former lover
happened: Tom: laughs low with Clara in a corner of the party, his hand on her arm, and does not see you come in.
remember: Tom told you last month that he still thinks about Clara sometimes.

situations.about: You are twelve.
situations.people: Maya, your best friend (you like them)
happened: Maya: sits with the new girl at lunch, in your usual seat, and they share earphones.

situations.inspired_by: envy as wanting what another has (Parrott and Smith, 1993)
happened: Your colleague: is announced as the new head of department -- the post you applied for and have wanted for years.

situations.about: Your family has rented the same cramped flat for fifteen years.
happened: Your school friend: shows you around her new house, with a garden and a room for each of her children.

situations.inspired_by: guilt, focused on the act and wanting repair (Tangney's TOSCA)
happened: Noor: calls from the vet -- her cat is dehydrated and sick, because you forgot to go and feed him while she was away.

situations.inspired_by: guilt at a worry one caused (ISEAR guilt antecedents)
situations.about: Last night you told your mother you were at the library; you were at a party, and your phone died.
happened: Your mother: opens the door in tears -- she spent the night calling hospitals.

situations.inspired_by: awkwardness (Cowen and Keltner, 2017); embarrassment at a public pratfall
happened: Climbing the stage to accept your award, you trip on the top step and sprawl at the presenter's feet in front of four hundred people.

situations.about: You are fourteen.
happened: You put up your hand and ask, 'Mom, can I go to the bathroom?' -- and the whole class turns to stare at you and your teacher.

situations.inspired_by: shame, focused on the self (Tangney's TOSCA)
situations.about: You won the regional chess title last month.
happened: The federation: announces that you used an engine in the final and plays the evidence to the hall; your coach looks away.

situations.inspired_by: authentic pride at an earned achievement (Tracy and Robins, 2007)
situations.about: A year ago you could not run a mile.
happened: You cross the marathon finish line; the clock says three hours fifty, and your daughter is screaming your name.

situations.inspired_by: sadness at a lost hope (ISEAR sadness antecedents)
situations.about: You have wanted to study at the conservatory since you were nine.
happened: The letter: regrets to inform you that the conservatory cannot offer you a place.

situations.people: Ruth, your closest friend (you like them)
happened: Ruth: hugs you goodbye at the farewell dinner; tomorrow she moves to the other side of the world.
You open your front door and forty people shout 'Surprise!' under a banner with your name on it.

situations.about: You were adopted as a baby.
happened: A letter from the adoption agency: says you have a twin brother, and that he has asked to meet you.

situations.inspired_by: Rocky (the vow to go the distance)
situations.about: Nobody expects you to last three rounds against the champion.
happened: Your trainer: asks, quietly, whether you want to call it off.
remember: You promised yourself that whatever happens, you will still be standing at the final bell.

situations.about: You have decided to open your grandmother's bakery again by Christmas, whatever it takes.
happened: The floodwater drains from the bakery, leaving mud to the counters.

situations.inspired_by: All Quiet on the Western Front; emotional numbing (Litz and Gray, 2002)
situations.about: You have been at the front for two years; lately nothing reaches you.
happened: The shell lands on the dugout next to yours; when the dust settles you step over what is left of the men you ate breakfast with.

situations.about: It is your ninth night shift in a row in the intensive care unit.
happened: The monitor on bed four flatlines; you note the time, finish the paperwork, and move on to bed five.

situations.inspired_by: nostalgia induction (Wildschut, Sedikides, Arndt and Routledge, 2006)
happened: Clearing the attic, you find your diary from the summer you were sixteen, a pressed daisy still between the pages.
remember: That summer at the lake you and your cousins swam every day and slept on the porch.

happened: The taxi radio plays the song everyone danced to the year you finished school.

situations.about: You have come home after twenty years at war and at sea.
happened: Your old dog, grey and thin by the gate, lifts his head at your voice, wags once, and dies.
remember: You raised him from a puppy before you left.

happened: Clearing the attic, you find your late brother's old jacket, still smelling of his cigarettes.
remember: Your brother died two years ago today.

situations.inspired_by: The Remains of the Day (the question answered with the silver)
happened: A letter from Miss Kenton: says she is happy enough with her husband, and sometimes thinks of what might have been.
remember: Twenty years ago she asked whether there was any reason for her to stay, and you talked about the silver.

happened: The news: reports that a small company has just been bought for a billion dollars, and its first staff are all rich.
remember: Ten years ago you turned down their offer to join, because it seemed too risky.

situations.about: You have been at war for three years.
situations.people: Ada, your wife, far away (you like them)
happened: A letter from Ada: arrives smelling faintly of her lavender, telling you the peach tree bloomed.
A postcard arrives from your closest friend, who moved abroad last spring.
remember: You used to see her every day.

situations.about: It is your first night at a boarding school three hundred miles from home; you are eleven.
happened: Unpacking, you find your mother has tucked a bar of her soap into your pillowcase, and the smell is home.

situations.about: You left your village in the mountains eight years ago and have not been back.
happened: A street vendor: sings, under her breath, the harvest song your grandmother used to sing.

situations.inspired_by: a past that will not let go (intrusive memory)
happened: The bus takes a detour over the old river bridge.
remember: Twenty years ago your brother drowned when the car went off this bridge, and you were driving.

situations.about: You served two tours as a combat medic.
happened: Fireworks crack over the park, and for a moment you are back in the burning convoy.
The sun is out, your friends have brought your favourite cake, and your test results came back clear this morning.
Your tooth throbs, the train was cancelled, and rain is coming in through the hole in your shoe.
You wake before the alarm after ten hours of sleep, the coffee is strong, and the day is wide open.
You finish your second shift in a row at four in the morning, and your legs will barely carry you to the car.

situations.about: You defuse bombs for a living.
happened: The timer reads forty seconds, and you still cannot tell which wire feeds the detonator.
You sway in a hammock between two palms, a cold drink in hand, with nothing to do until dinner.

situations.about: You captain a sailing ship.
happened: You call the tack, and the crew move as one; the ship comes about exactly where you wanted her.
The bank changed the locks on your house this morning; your appeal was refused and there is no one left to call.

situations.inspired_by: insight, the pieces falling into place
situations.about: You are a detective who has worked this case for a month.
happened: The torn ticket stub in the victim's glove makes everything fall into place: you know exactly who did it, and how.
You wake in a room you have never seen, in clothes that are not yours, with no memory of the last two days.

situations.people: your parents, your brothers and your grandmother (you like them)
happened: Your brother: starts the old family joke about the burnt turkey, and the whole table joins in, word for word.

situations.about: You moved to a city of eight million people a month ago and still know nobody.
happened: Your birthday comes and goes; the only message is from your phone company.

situations.people: Rosa, your oldest friend (you like them)
happened: Rosa: sits with you on the porch late at night and asks what has really been wrong, and you find yourself telling her everything.
A stranger in a grey suit: asks where you were on Tuesday night, who you were with, and why you are sweating.
Your children: ambush you with snowballs from behind the car, shrieking with laughter.

situations.about: You are a judge.
happened: The defendant stands for sentencing, and the courtroom falls silent.
Your oncologist: says the tumour has shrunk by half, and the treatment is working.
The last lifeboat pulls away from the sinking ship without you, and the deck tilts under your feet.
The storm howls outside, but the doors are locked, the fire is lit, and your family is asleep upstairs.
Footsteps follow you down the dark alley, stopping whenever you stop.
You have been lost in the chess problem for three hours; the solution is close, and the rest of the world has disappeared.
The meeting about stationery enters its fourth hour, and the chair begins another slide on paper clips.
A bully: shoves your little brother against the lockers, and you step forward between them.
Men with torches search the barn below while you hold your breath in the hayloft, praying they do not look up.

situations.about: You have kept the lighthouse alone for six weeks.
happened: The supply boat rounds the point, and you can see faces on deck.

situations.about: You have spent twelve hours hosting your sister's wedding for two hundred guests.
happened: The last guest leaves, and the house is quiet at last.

situations.about: You are fifteen.
happened: On the last night of summer camp, everyone sits around the dying fire singing the camp song one final time.
Marcus: struts out onto the icy steps in his new Italian shoes and lands flat on his backside.
remember: Marcus has mocked your work in front of the whole office all year.

happened: Elise: puts the engagement ring on the table between you and says she cannot marry you.
Your boss: reads your report aloud at the all-staff meeting as an example of what not to do, and the room laughs.

situations.inspired_by: a feeding creature and a willing lover: craving and sexual desire together (the owner's feeding stories)
situations.about: You are a creature who feeds on the life of your lovers, and you have not fed in days.
happened: Your chosen one slips into your bed, eager and unaware.

situations.inspired_by: an invitation into a crowd (for person types)
happened: A friend: invites you to a party tonight with a hundred people you have never met.

situations.people: Jamie, your partner of two years (you like them)
happened: Jamie: says they need some space for a while, and does not say how long.
Your boss: stops by your desk to say your report was the best she has read this year.

situations.inspired_by: a lone stranger unaware of being watched (for person types)
happened: A lone hiker sits by the trail, humming, unaware of you watching from the trees.
Sky: has booked two tickets to a country neither of you has ever visited, leaving tomorrow at dawn.
The clerk stamps your form and calls the next number.
The bus arrives two minutes late, as it usually does, on a mild grey morning.
The instructions say to fit panel B into slot C before tightening the screws.

situations.inspired_by: The Treasure of the Sierra Madre (the partners' gold)
situations.people: Curtin and Howard, your partners in the mine
happened: Your partners sleep; the three sacks of gold dust sit by the fire, and you are the only one awake.
remember: It took ten months of digging to fill them.

situations.inspired_by: A Christmas Carol (the counting-house on Christmas Eve)
situations.about: You have spent your life making money and keeping it.
happened: Your clerk: asks, shivering, whether he might put one more lump of coal on his fire, while you count the day's takings.

situations.inspired_by: a generous act (a near-miss for greed)
happened: A child: shivers at the bus stop in a thin shirt, and you take off your coat and wrap it around her.
On an empty late train you find a wallet on the seat beside you, fat with cash, the owner's card inside.

situations.inspired_by: cruelty by the powerful to the powerless (the Doctor's learned cue)
happened: A guard: kicks a chained, starving prisoner who asked for water, and laughs.

situations.inspired_by: a survivor's cue: questions about home and family
happened: A child: asks where you are from, and whether your family misses you.

situations.people: Amara, your travelling companion (you like them)
happened: Amara: says she is not going home after all -- she wants to keep travelling with you.
A metallic voice: announces over every speaker in the city that its population will be exterminated at dawn.

situations.inspired_by: a cue on Isolde's card: praise of another's 'gift' or 'genius'
happened: The director: tells the orchestra that the newcomer's overture is the work of a true genius -- a gift that cannot be taught.

situations.inspired_by: a cue on Celestine's card: the smell of cheap wine and tobacco
happened: The smell of cheap wine and pipe tobacco drifts out of a tavern doorway as you pass.

situations.inspired_by: a cue on Varga's card: praise for his integrity
happened: A young officer: raises his cup and toasts you as the most honourable man he has ever served under.

situations.inspired_by: a cue on Varga's card: a soldier asking about patrol routes
happened: A soldier: asks you, casually, who else knows the patrol routes this week.

situations.inspired_by: a cue on Wren's card: being told she is young
happened: An older neighbour: pats your hand and says you are too young to know what you want.

situations.inspired_by: a cue on Wren's card: tar and salt
happened: Passing the boatyard, you smell hot tar and salt on the wind.

situations.inspired_by: a cue on Anselm's card: woodsmoke
happened: Woodsmoke from a cookfire drifts in under the door.

situations.inspired_by: a cue on Aldo's card: his daughter packing a bag
happened: Your daughter: is packing a bag in her room, humming.

situations.inspired_by: a cue on Aldo's card: an offer to help with physical labour
happened: A young man: offers to carry your crate up the quay for you.

situations.inspired_by: a cue on Holt's card: a witness who answers too fluently
situations.about: You are taking a witness's statement.
happened: The witness: answers every question smoothly, in exactly the order you asked them, without a pause.

situations.inspired_by: a cue on Holt's card: 'surely you can see your way to...'
situations.about: You are a magistrate.
happened: The mill owner: leans in and says, 'Surely you can see your way to a quicker verdict.'

situations.inspired_by: a cue on Margit's card: a kindness without strings
happened: You find a basket of eggs on your doorstep, from a neighbour, with no note.

situations.inspired_by: the caregiving behavioural system (Bowlby, 1969; George and Solomon, 1996)
situations.people: Ben, your six-year-old nephew (you love him)
happened: A big dog, off its lead, runs snarling across the park straight at Ben.

situations.inspired_by: bystander intervention (Latane and Darley, 1970); Stand By Me
situations.people: Sam, your small younger friend (you like him); Rob, a much bigger boy
happened: Rob: shoves Sam against the lockers and snatches his bag while two others laugh.

situations.inspired_by: affectionate love at rest (the intimacy of Sternberg's triangle)
happened: Tom: falls asleep against your shoulder on the sofa, breathing slow, the film still playing.

situations.inspired_by: anticipatory anxiety under uncertainty (Grupe and Nitschke, 2013)
happened: A nurse calls: the scan results are back, and the doctor wants to see you in person tomorrow at nine to discuss them.
remember: Your mother's illness began with a call like this.

situations.inspired_by: the wait before a verdict (Twelve Angry Men; anticipatory anxiety)
happened: Your lawyer says the jury has sent word: they will return their verdict after lunch.
remember: The prosecutor asked for ten years.

situations.inspired_by: the confidence trick; cues to deception (DePaulo et al., 2003)
situations.people: a stranger in a smart coat
happened: The stranger: insists on carrying your suitcase to the platform, asks which carriage you are in and where you are staying, and keeps glancing at your handbag.

situations.inspired_by: a breach of trust in a partnership (Glengarry Glen Ross)
situations.people: Martin, your business partner (you like him)
happened: Martin: says the missing four thousand was a bank error, will not show you the statement, and changes the subject to the weather.

situations.inspired_by: trust in close relationships (Rempel, Holmes and Zanna, 1985)
situations.people: Jo, your oldest friend (you like her)
happened: Jo: offers to hold your wallet and keys while you swim, and waves you into the sea.

situations.inspired_by: watchfulness on sentry duty (All Quiet on the Western Front)
happened: On the wall at midnight, word comes down the line that enemy scouts were seen in the valley an hour ago. Somewhere below, a branch snaps.

situations.inspired_by: clinical watchfulness through the night (the night nurse)
situations.people: Mr Hale, your patient (you like him)
happened: Two hours after his surgery, Mr Hale's heart monitor skips a beat, steadies, then skips again.
The last train home leaves in four minutes, and you are still two streets from the station with a heavy suitcase.

situations.inspired_by: an emergency that waits for no one (triage)
happened: Leo: slices his forearm on broken glass; blood is pooling fast on the kitchen floor, and the nearest doctor is across town.
The last dovetail joint of the cabinet slides home with a soft push: tight, square, not a hair of light through it.
Halfway through a hard operation, the last artery is tied off cleanly; your hands are steady and the bleeding stops exactly as you planned.
Your raffle ticket, bought on a whim, wins a basket of cheeses and a bottle of wine.

situations.inspired_by: victory over a rival (Rocky; hubristic and authentic pride, Tracy and Robins, 2007)
situations.people: Viktor, who beat you in the final three years running
happened: Viktor: tips over his king and offers his hand; you have won the championship.
The council chairman stands up at the meeting and admits, in front of everyone, that you were right about the dam all along and they were wrong to mock you.

situations.inspired_by: relief as a threat removed (Sweeny and Vohs, 2012)
happened: The doctor calls: the lump was benign, and there is nothing more to do.
remember: You have not slept properly since the scan.

situations.inspired_by: reunion after separation (the attachment system; Home Alone)
situations.people: Mia, your four-year-old daughter (you love her)
happened: A steward brings Mia to the lost-children tent, sticky with candyfloss and perfectly fine, an hour after she went missing at the fair.

situations.inspired_by: low-arousal positive affect (the circumplex, Russell, 1980; Tsai's ideal affect)
happened: The harvest is in. You sit on the porch with a cup of tea as the light goes gold over the fields; nothing needs doing until morning.

situations.inspired_by: warmth after a shared meal (Little Women's Christmas)
happened: Dinner is over; everyone is full and warm, laughing softly around the table while the fire settles.
You take the first spoonful of the plum pudding you wait all year for, and make yourself eat it slowly so it lasts.

situations.inspired_by: savoring a last time (Bryant and Veroff, 2007)
happened: On the last evening of the holiday you sit on the warm rocks and watch the sun go down over the sea, not wanting it to end.
